newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico, Zapatistas to restart peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, Zapatistas to restart peace talks.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1996-11-04

text.p: Mexican government negotiators and Zapatista guerrillas will meet on Tuesday for the first time in more than two months, rekindling a stalled peace process, officials said.
The two sides will install a special commission to oversee peace accords once they are signed.

The Zapatista National Liberation Army (EZLN), a Maya Indian-based rebel force from the southeastern state of Chiapas, launched an armed uprising on New Year's Day 1994, and has been in on-and-off peace talks with the government for 19 months.

Setting up the new commission will meet one of the Zapatista demands for returning to proper talks. The Zapatistas unilaterally suspended negotiations on Sept. 2, claiming the government team was intransigent and racist.
Among the other Zapatista demands for returning to talks were the release of 17 sympathisers from jail. The government freed seven of them over the weekend on bail.

dc.value: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico
